primary.title: Log-Concave Sampling
primary.author: Sinho Chewi
primary.role: Primary theorem order and source-facing statement authority.

official_supplement.title: Supplement to Log-Concave Sampling
official_supplement.author: Sinho Chewi
official_supplement.role: Official material omitted from the book for space; treated as source material for Chapter 2, not as an ASTIS invention.

sections.title: Proof of Marton's tensorization
sections.summary: Marton's product-space tensorization of transport inequalities, proved by induction using conditional couplings and the KL chain rule.
items: Theorem 1.1: Marton's tensorization

sections.title: Concentration of measure
sections.summary: Concentration around means and medians, the Herbst entropy-to-mgf argument, and transport-inequality characterizations of concentration.
items: 1.2.1 Equivalence between the mean and the median
Lemma 1.2: Herbst argument
Theorem 1.2: concentration from Poincare and log-Sobolev inequalities
Theorem 1.3: Bobkov-Gotze equivalence between T1 and sub-Gaussian concentration
Theorem 1.4: T1 is equivalent to Gaussian integrability of a distance function

sections.title: Tensorization and Gozlan's theorem
sections.summary: Explains how tensorization creates dimension-free concentration and proves the converse route from product-space concentration to the T2 transport inequality.
items: Lemma 1.3: empirical-measure Wasserstein Lipschitz bound and Wasserstein law of large numbers
Theorem 1.5: Sanov's theorem, used as a black box
Theorem 1.6: Gozlan's equivalence between T2 and dimension-free sub-Gaussian concentration

sections.title: Metric measure spaces
sections.summary: Extends the Chapter 2 curvature discussion from smooth manifolds to metric-measure geometry and compares the optimal-transport and Bakry-Emery viewpoints.
items: 1.4.1 Metric geometry: length, geodesic spaces, model spaces, and Alexandrov curvature
1.4.2 Lott-Sturm-Villani synthetic Ricci curvature and displacement convexity of entropy
Definition 1.7: measured Gromov-Hausdorff convergence
Theorem 1.7: stability of synthetic Ricci curvature bounds
1.4.3 Discussion: scope of the results and the relation between Bakry-Emery and optimal-transport curvature

sections.title: Exercises
sections.summary: Exercises complete several proof details and connect the supplement to classical concentration inequalities.
items: Exercise 1.1: Herbst argument and the Poincare concentration case
Exercise 1.2: Hoeffding's lemma and Pinsker's inequality
Exercise 1.3: bounded differences / Azuma-Hoeffding
Exercise 1.4: empirical Wasserstein Lipschitz bound used in Gozlan's theorem
Exercise 1.5: Poincare and T1 are incomparable

primary.title: First-Order Methods in Optimization
primary.author: Amir Beck
primary.role: Primary chapter spine for the First-Order Optimization Library.

supplement.title: Lectures on Optimization
supplement.author: Sinho Chewi
supplement.role: Supplementary theorem-proof exposition and cross-check for Beck; it does not replace Beck as the primary source. Chewi states that these notes are primarily based on Bubeck (2015), Beck (2017), and Nesterov (2018).

2.note: Extended-valued convex analysis and Fenchel duality provide the closest supplementary treatment.

5.note: Smoothness, strong convexity, gradient flow/descent, acceleration, and convexity-smoothness duality.

7.note: Symmetric-matrix background is relevant; Beck remains the primary treatment of spectral functions.

9.note: Bregman divergences, relative convexity/smoothness, mirror methods, and online algorithms.

10.note: Proximal methods plus the unified stochastic mirror proximal-gradient theorem.

11.note: Alternating minimization is related to block methods, but this is not treated as an exact chapter equivalence.

12.note: Proximal structure together with Fenchel duality.

14.note: Alternating projections, convergence of alternating minimization, and entropic OT case study.

15.note: Beck remains the primary source for ADMM; Chewi's notes are not presented as a substitute.
